text:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a speculative-decoding prototype on llama3-13b (8-bit q5) this morning. seeing ~1.8x token/s on synthetic chat load but small quality dips on closed-book items. attaching quick notes.

linus: awesome, can you paste the exact config?

maya: sure — short snippet:

```
model: llama3-13b-q5
sampling: top_k=40, temp=0.7
speculative: enabled
speculative_workers: 4
speculative_threshold: 0.25  # prob ratio threshold for accept
fallback_policy: greedy_top1
kv_cache: align_shards=true
```

zara: did you include early-exit or any token-level accept heuristics?

maya: no early-exit. the speculative path accepts proposals when model-B's top token prob * threshold > model-A's prob. simple heuristic for the prototype.

sam: what's the eval harness? we need consistent sampling to measure quality impact. can you run deterministic comparison (greedy) and sampling match with fixed seeds?

maya: ran two suites:
- deterministic (greedy) baseline float16 A100
- speculative q5 run (same prompts, seeded sampling)
Observed: throughput +82%, median per-token latency slightly lower, p95 latency +10ms because of extra checks.
Quality: on MMLU microbench (subset) accuracy drop 1.3 percentage points vs float16 greedy. on HumanEval-style code tasks, pass@1 flat.

linus: 1.3% is non-trivial. could be sampling noise. how many prompts / tokens?

maya: ~18k prompts, avg 120 tokens each. repeated 2 runs. seeds kept same where relevant but some nondeterminism from quantized kernels.

zara: can we isolate the quantization vs speculative logic? run:
1) float16 + speculative (no q5)
2) q5 + no-speculative
3) q5 + speculative (current)
That will tell us interaction effects.

maya: planned — queued those jobs on bench cluster. ETA ~4h.

sam: we should also test different speculative_thresholds (0.1, 0.25, 0.5) and measure precision/accept rates. small threshold -> more accepts -> more perf but higher risk.

maya: agreed. preliminary accept rates: threshold 0.25 -> 42% accepted, 0.1 -> 68% accepted (failed more often), 0.5 -> 18% accepted.

linus: important to log where fallbacks happen. please add counters: proposals_total, accepted_by_threshold, accepted_but_mismatch (when accepted token != gold token), fallback_triggered.

maya: added metrics to runtime: spec.proposals_total, spec.accepted, spec.mismatch_rate, spec.fallback_count. pushed to prometheus under exp.spec.*.

eval-bot: CI:bench/2793141592 posted — full run artifacts at https://ci.internal.redwood/bench/2793141592 (results to be uploaded automatically).

zara: for canary: suggest 0.5% traffic for 24h, monitor token-level mismatch_rate, top-10 prompts with highest mismatch, p50/p95 latency, and end-to-end user error rates. auto-rollback if mismatch_rate > 2% or end-to-end error spike.

sam: add qualitative checks — sample 200 generation pairs and run small human review. canary needs both metric and QA gate.

maya: I also noticed an odd pattern: when context length > 1024, speculative accept rate drops ~10% and mismatch rate rises slightly. might be kv-cache alignment/quantization drift.

linus: that smells like sharded kv precision differences. try forcing single-shard kv for the experiment and compare.

maya: will do. next steps: finish isolation runs (float16 vs q5), sweep thresholds, run single-shard kv test, then prepare canary plan doc. posting quick log snippets in the bench link.

zara: thanks — please tag me when the q5 vs float16 runs finish. also include sample prompts that triggered regressions so we can build a focused eval set. :eyes:

maya: will do. tl;dr: promising perf wins but need to validate quality across quantization and context-length corners before rolling out.

sam: sounds good. ping once artifacts are in. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks everyone — will update thread when jobs complete.
